newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly says earnings jump 11 percent.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly says earnings jump 11 percent.

text.p: Eli Lilly & Co. reported Monday an 11 percent rise in first-quarter earnings and said new products would fuel its growth.
The drug giant said it earned $432.6 million, or 79 cents a share, vs. year-earlier earnings of $389.2 million, or 71 cents a share.
Revenues rose to $1.95 billion from $1.78 billion.
Lilly said its earnings would have been ever higher had it not been for a $24 million charge to discontinue a collaboration arrangement with biotechnology firm Somatogen Inc.
Excluding that charge, its would have earned 82 cents a share, it said.
"The introduction of new products and additional indications for existing products will drive our future sales growth," said Randall Tobias, chairman and chief executive officer.
"Our sales growth and strict expense controls helped us realise our first-quarter operating income growth of 21 percent. We will continue to focus on this priority," he said.
Worldwide sales for the quarter were $1.95 billion, up 10 percent from the first quarter of 1996, though global selling prices were hurt by unfavourable foreign exchange fluctuations, it said.
Eli Lilly's stock was off $1 at $84 in early morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
